deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous one, which set up a 'mobility index' for points of a locally finite-dimensional space X. A point x is ν-mobile in X if, near x, X is a product (R^ν × N', (0,o)), i.e. X is equisingular along a ν-dimensional manifold germ through x. The mobility index v(x) is the largest such ν. The sets Y_ν(X) = v^{-1}(ν) are the 'strata' of what is in effect a canonical intrinsic stratification. Props A–C on the previous page conjecture that these Y_ν are manifolds of codimension ν, that X is a local product along them, and that they are maximal.

Prop D (this page): let Y be a topological manifold of pure dimension i and N any topological space. For (y,n) in Y×N and ν ≥ i, the claim is that (y,n) is ν-mobile in Y×N iff n is (ν−i)-mobile in N. Hence Y_ν(Y×N) = Y × Y_{ν−i}(N): the mobility stratification is compatible with products by manifolds and shifts indices by dim Y. Every point of Y×N is automatically i-mobile.

Left margin, first note: N 'dévissable' ⟺ Y×N 'dévissable' (for Y ≠ ∅). Here 'dévissable' is the property, mentioned on the previous page, of admitting such a stratification.

Left margin, second note: 'Prop B ⇐ (sous réserve de Prop A)'. That is, Prop D is meant to deliver the local-product statement Prop B, provided Prop A holds.

Purpose: these are the axioms of an intrinsic, 'tame' stratification, as part of Grothendieck's 1974 'topologie modérée' programme. Product compatibility is a basic property any such canonical stratification should have.
errors: The 'if' direction is trivial: a local splitting N ≅ R^{ν−i}×N' gives Y×N ≅ R^ν×N' locally. The 'only if' direction is a germ-cancellation statement and is FALSE for arbitrary topological spaces N. Counterexample from the Cannon–Edwards double suspension theorem (late 1970s, after this note): let H be the Poincaré homology 3-sphere and N = c(H), the open cone with vertex o. Then R^2 × c(H) ≅ c(Σ^2 H) ≅ R^6, so (y,o) has mobility 6. But o is not a manifold point of N, so it is not 4-mobile. Prop D therefore needs a tameness hypothesis on N (e.g. PL/polyhedral or o-minimal). In the polyhedral setting the expected analogue is the product behaviour of the intrinsic stratification of polyhedra (Armstrong, Akin); I have not checked this.
Consequently the margin equivalence 'N dévissable ⟺ Y×N dévissable' is also only plausible in a tame category. The direction Y×N ⇒ N is the one at risk.
The statement only treats ν ≥ i, which is fine since every point of Y×N is at least i-mobile.

ideas.what: Mobility index / intrinsic stratification defined by maximal local product splitting R^ν × (N,o), and its behaviour under products with an i-manifold (index shifts by i)
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic (coarsest) stratification / intrinsic filtration; product formula for intrinsic strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan, Armstrong and Akin (polyhedra, ~1968–69); H. King (topological intrinsic filtration, 1985); discussed further in G. Friedman's 'Singular Intersection Homology'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches tame topology and canonical 'dévissage' of stratified spaces, but not this specific product statement as far as I know

ideas.what: Stability of 'dévissability' (admitting the canonical stratification) under products with a nonempty manifold
ideas.modern_name: Product stability of stratifiability / pseudomanifold classes

missed.claim: Grothendieck states product compatibility of the intrinsic mobility stratification for arbitrary topological N. This fails topologically because of the double suspension phenomenon, which was unknown in 1974. The page thus implicitly shows why a 'tame' (modérée) framework is required for intrinsic stratifications. This is the same issue later met for King's intrinsic filtration, but it is not a new result.
missed.quote: Si ν ≥ i, (y,n) ∈ Y×N est ν-mobile ssi n∈N est (ν−i)-mobile. Donc Y_ν(Y×N) = Y×Y_{ν−i}(N).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical illustration that Grothendieck's tame-topology axioms (Props A–D) must exclude topological pathologies such as R^2 × c(H) ≅ R^6. It is relevant to o-minimal and tame settings, where such product/cancellation properties should hold.

deep.surprise_reason: A short, natural lemma on how an intrinsic stratification behaves under products. It is routine in tame settings and actually false in full topological generality, a fact Grothendieck could not know in 1974. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of the 1974 tame-topology sketch.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit Y [...] un espace topologique partout de dim i' should read 'Soit Y une variété topologique partout de dim i', i.e. Y is a topological manifold.
Margin: 'N dénombrable[?] ⟺ Y×N dénombrable[?]' is more likely 'N dévissable ⟺ Y×N dévissable (Y≠∅)', consistent with 'dévissable' on the previous page.
Margin: 'Prop B ⇐ (conséquence[?] de Prop A)' appears to read 'Prop B ⇐ (sous réserve de Prop A)'.
